title.narrative: BO Road Sector Capacity Development Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives (PDO) are to enhance Bolivia's national road sector management and improve the condition of the country's primary paved road network targeted under the Project.

The objectives of the Road Sector Capacity Development Project for Bolivia are to enhance Bolivia's national road sector management and improve the condition of the country's primary paved road network targeted under the Project. There are two components to the project, the first component being capacity development. The additional activities listed below will be financed but through transactional-based disbursement (US$5 million): implementation of an integrated FM information system, strengthening ABC's environmental and social management capacity concerning road works (US$1.0 million), and development of a rehabilitation planning strategy for the paved primary road network (US$1.5 million). The second component is the road contracting for paved primary network. Under this subcomponent, bidding documents for the rehabilitation and maintenance works contracts to be financed under part B.2 below will be prepared through, inter alia: (a) the provision of transactional advice and validation of design and costs for said works; and (b) the carrying out of awareness campaigns of the potential effects of using performance-based contracts.

comment.narrative: To estimate direct project beneficiaries, the methodology considered the population of the 12 municipalities traversed by the Santa Cruz–Trinidad road: El Puente, Ascensión de Guarayos, Cuatro Cañadas, San Javier, San Julián, San Ramón, Cotoca, Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Pailón, San AndrEs, Trinidad, and San Javier. As rehabilitation and maintenance works were completed across all five civil works lots—covering the road segments through these municipalities—the indicator was achieved. Population data were sourced from the 2022 National Institute of Statistics census. It is important to note that this estimation approach is conservative, as it excludes users from outside these municipalities who regularly travel along the corridor. Therefore, the actual number of direct beneficiaries is likely significantly higher than reported.

ABC implemented a citizen engagement system through inclusive dissemination and information-sharing activities related to project preparation and implementation, in line with the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP). This included the socialization of environmental and social plans developed under the project. A key focus of these efforts was to ensure the participation of vulnerable groups. ABC monitored the proportion of participants representing vulnerable groups in these engagement processes. Out of a total of 317 participants in citizen engagement activities, 133 were identified as vulnerable individuals—representing 41.97 percent. This exceeds the project's target of 30 percent. Disaggregated by lot, the participation rates of vulnerable groups were as follows: Lot 1 – 48%, Lot 2 – 44%, Lot 3 – 39%, Lot 4 – 41%, and Lot 5 – 36%. These results demonstrate that the target was surpassed across all project lots.

The total length of roads rehabilitated and maintained under the project amounts to 564.61 km, with all civil works completed by project closing. The breakdown by lot is as follows: Lot 1 – 74.76 km; Lot 2 – 61.15 km; Lot 3 – 106.40 km; Lot 4 – 182.71 km; and Lot 5 – 139.59 km. This confirms that the full rehabilitation scope was successfully delivered.

title.narrative: Average International Roughness Index (IRI) of target roads at contract closings is less than 3 m per km.

comment.narrative: At project closing, the monitoring firm measured the International Roughness Index (IRI) along every kilometer of the five civil works lots and calculated a weighted average for each. The corridor-wide average was 2.06?m per km, exceeding the end target of 3.00?m per km. Disaggregated results were as follows: Lot 1 (74.76?km) averaged 2.66?m per km; Lot 2 (61.15?km), 1.90?m per km; Lot 3 (106.40?km), 2.50?m per km; Lot 4 (182.71?km), 1.71?m per km; and Lot 5 (139.59?km), 1.89?m per km. Within Lot 5, roughness varied significantly: the Nueva Cocota–Trinidad segment (101.50?km) recorded 1.47?m per km; Trinidad–Puerto Varador (12.89?km), 1.91?m per km; while Trinidad–San Javier (25.20?km) registered 3.55?m per km. This last segment, which accounts for only 4.5 percent of the total corridor length, remained above the IRI target. Nonetheless, the overall corridor average comfortably met the intended standard.

title.narrative: ABC's Socio-environmental Manual updated and approved

comment.narrative: This indicator was achieved in July 2020. The activity included the preparation of (i) the Manual for the Release of Rights of Way and (ii) the Guide for Community Participation and Engagement. ABC received support from CAF in carrying out this activity.

title.narrative: Conceptual design of a financial management system

comment.narrative: This intermediate indicator is directly linked to PDO Indicator 1. ABC completed the conceptual design of the financial management system by December 2023. However, at that time, the indicator was not considered achieved, as it originally required the design to be for an “integrated” system encompassing all planned functionalities—budgeting, financial management, procurement, monitoring, and contract management—within a single platform. The indicator was revised during the second project restructuring in May 2024 to remove the reference to “integrated,” recognizing instead the improvements in ABC's financial management capacity. Following this adjustment, the intermediate indicator was deemed achieved.

title.narrative: Pavement Management System installed and populated with information related to the primary paved network

comment.narrative: This intermediate indicator is linked to PDO Indicator 2. It was achieved in August 2023. The IDB supported the conceptual design and installation of the Pavement Management System, which is also associated with DLI 3.1. The system was successfully populated with data on the primary paved network, thereby meeting the indicator's requirements.

title.narrative: Development of an ABC strategy for primary highway network rehabilitation planning by the purchase and installation of a Pavement Management System and populating it with pertinent data.

comment.narrative: By end-2024, ABC had achieved the objective of developing a strategy for paved primary highway network rehabilitation planning. With support from the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), ABC installed a Pavement Management System (PMS) in August 2023 and trained 23 technical staff—well above the original target of three. Project funds subsequently supported the population of the PMS with road condition data covering 90 percent of the paved primary network by March 2024, along with an update for 20 percent of that network by year-end. These efforts enabled ABC to prepare a data-driven methodology for prioritizing road investments based on PMS outputs. A pilot investment plan, applying this methodology, was also developed for the Bioceanic Highway. The pilot confirmed the methodology's effectiveness across diverse terrain, climates, and pavement types.

title.narrative: A financial management Information System in ABC detailed, designed, installed, and used.

comment.narrative: This outcome reflects that ABC, to the satisfaction of the Bank, has: (i) approved the conceptual design of the financial management information system; (ii) developed and approved the system; and (iii) installed and operationalized it. The target was achieved by mid-2024, with ABC successfully deploying and using the SICOPP financial management system. This system enhances ABC's institutional capacity by providing accurate financial data to support core business operations. Additionally, ABC conducted training for its staff to ensure effective use of the system.
